thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU queue growth detected in eu-west1 cluster 'gw-prod-gpu'. Autoscaler saturated at max_nodes=48, queue length rising > 1200. Severity: P1 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Pager triggered for on-call: @alex (SRE) — escalation to P1.

alex: I'm on it. Observability shows sustained enqueue rate ~400 rps and token-level backlog. 95th latency up x6 in last 10m.

maria: Any customer-facing errors? I'm seeing an uptick in 429s and a few 503s on dedicated tenants.

julian: Runtime driver logs show repeated CUDA/Xid errors on several nodes and OOMs in the driver process, causing the node agent to drift into restart loops. Suspect these nodes are being marked unhealthy and reducing effective GPU count.

eng-runtime: Confirmed stack traces: repeated 'Xid 13' followed by 'GPU process killed' and kernel messages. Happened right after a driver hotpatch rolled out ~00:40 UTC.

alex: That would explain autoscaler not catching up — nodes come up but then immediately fail healthchecks and never register GPUs. Autoscaler sees nodes but not capacity.

ops: We're at max_nodes because of a quota limit on the account for eu-west1 GPUs. Terraform shows quota cap at 48. Requesting emergency quota bump now but won't be instant.

maria: Customer impact: internal dashboard shows ~12% of production requests falling into retry/backoff paths. Key enterprise tenants on Dedicated are experiencing degraded tail latency and some throttles. I'll draft a short status for customers once we have mitigation.

alex: Immediate plan: 1) Reduce non-critical workloads to free capacity (throttle batch/low-priority queues). 2) Roll back the driver hotpatch to the previous stable image on the affected pools. 3) Temporarily raise autoscaler max to 72 (if quota allowed) and spin up emergency spare nodes in eu-central as cross-region fallback. 4) Cordon and drain the flaky nodes to stop restart churn.

julian: I'll own driver rollback. Rolling back via our rollout tool now. Command:```/rollout driver-image gw-prod-gpu --to-tag stable-2026-02-12```

eng-runtime: Reverting should remove the driver-level OOM/Xid pattern; prepping a config to disable the new kernel-sync optimization that correlates with the failure.

ops: Quota request submitted to cloud support with priority P0. But ETA ~20-30m. Spinning up eu-central spare nodes now as a stopgap.

alex: Throttling low-priority queue: applying a rate-limit at the router edge to reduce enqueue rate from 400 -> 260 rps. Command (internal):```curl -X POST https://router.internal/api/rate-limit -d '{"pool":"gpu-lowprio","limit_qps":0.5}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'```

eve: Adding temporary rule to route 30% of new requests to us-west1 to reduce strain. This will increase latency for those requests but keeps service live. Patching load-balancer now.

maria: Customer comms: sending initial notice saying 'We're experiencing GPU capacity issues in eu-west1 due to a driver regression; mitigation in progress. Some API requests may see higher latency, we're prioritizing critical workloads.' Will post as soon as rollback confirmed.

alex: Rollback progress: 3/5 affected node pools updated, healthchecks show registrations back to the serving pool for 2 of them. Event logs below:```[00:52:14] node-104: driver-restart -> healthy
[00:52:37] node-212: driver-restart -> healthy
[00:53:01] node-318: still Xid loop
```

julian: node-318 is flapping. I'll cordon and drain it:```kubectl cordon node-318
kubectl drain node-318 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n gpu-pool```

ops: eu-central spare nodes are registering but not yet at full capacity due to image bake time. Cheaper to shift non-critical traffic there for now.

eng-runtime: Observability shows Xid events drop by ~85% on pools with rollback applied. That's encouraging. Still seeing a few residual OOMs on older nodes — might be unrelated (memory leak in preemption handler).

alex: Manual autoscaler bump attempted but blocked by quota. As temporary, I've increased per-pool concurrency limits to avoid maxing single nodes: updating pool config to max_concurrency=18 -> 12 to spread load.

maria: Noting impacted tenants for post-incident review: tenant-alpha (dedicated), tenant-gamma (hosted, high traffic), internal-qa. Will open tickets and patch rough ETA into each ticket.

eve: LB reroute is live, moved ~28% of traffic to us-west1. Early signs: eu-west1 enqueue rate dropped 30% and backlog is flattening.

alex: Good. Next steps: continue rollback across remaining pools, finish cordon/drain of flapping nodes, and monitor queue for 30m. If Xid/OOM persists after rollback, we escalate to kernel team.

julian: Rollback complete on all targeted pools at 00:57 UTC. Post-rollback metrics: Xid events -> near zero, node restarts down to baseline.

eng-runtime: Kernel traces saved and uploaded to /artifacts/incident/5531234567/xid-traces.tar.gz for postmortem.

ops: Cloud quota increased (soft approval) to 68 for the account; added 12 spare GPUs — they are provisioning.

alex: Backpressure removed from low-prio router, but we will keep reduced concurrency for another 10m to ensure stability.

maria: Posting customer update: short note out to affected tenants mentioning rollback success and mitigation steps; include apology and offer support.

sre-lead: Great coordination. For the postmortem: collect exact time windows for Xid spike, driver rollout metadata, autoscaler behavior (why it thought nodes were available), and quota gating. Action items: stricter canary for driver, autoscaler should validate GPU registration not just node count, and pre-authorized emergency quota process.

alex: Marking incident as 'mitigated' at 00:59 UTC — backlog dropping, latency returning to expected levels, no new Xid events. Leaving thread open for 45m for monitoring.

maria: Filing status page update and follow-up postmortem draft. Assigning owners: julian (driver rollbacks & canary improvements), ops (quota and cross-region capacity), eng-runtime (investigate memory leak), alex (autoscaler validation change), maria (customer comms).

incident-bot: Incident mitigated by on-call actions. Duration: ~19 minutes. Tags: gpu, autoscaler, driver, xid, quota, rollback.

alex: Thanks everyone. If anything flares up ping me directly.

maria: I'll consolidate notes and close the incident channel after postmortem tasks created. :white_check_mark:
